First, where we stand. What went over the limit this month isn't storage, it's transfer, called egress. 11.45 gigabytes went out, more than twice the free 5 gigabyte limit. The database is only 112 megabytes. It jumped from October 18th, peaked at 2.27 gigabytes on the 23rd, and paying for Pro today lifted the block.

The API logs show one clear culprit. The staff tee sheet read the booking list 19,186 times in a day. Everything else is hundreds to a few thousand calls, mostly empty replies. Calls and egress rise and fall together, so each read is about 100 kilobytes.

The code shows why. Every 5 seconds the tee sheet re-reads a whole week of bookings, twelve times a minute, even when nothing changed. Opening the second sheet added on October 21st doubles it, and every PC and tab polls on its own. One screen open for twelve hours is about 0.86 gigabytes a day.

There are four levers: read less often, fetch only on change, fetch less data, and let the server push. The recommendation is the first two together. It's a one-day job with the biggest effect. The other two are for later, only if needed.

Step one: read less often. Go from 5 seconds to 30, and slow to 60 when nobody has touched the screen for two minutes. Your own save or payment still refreshes your screen right away. Only other PCs, phone and web bookings show up to 30 seconds later. That alone cuts about 83 percent.

Step two: full reload only on change. Every 5 seconds, ask for a tiny change stamp with the booking count and the latest edit time, and download the week only when the stamp changes. Holds expire on their own, so the stamp includes the earliest expiry too. It feels just as fast, and with step one it cuts 98 percent or more.

A few related spots. If the second sheet shows the same week as the left, share the result, and the starter screen gets the same stamp. The Fly server workers poll once a minute with near-empty replies, so leave them. Keep the spend cap on, and check the usage page once a week.

In short, the peak day's 2.27 gigabytes drops to 0.38 with step one, and to about 0.04 with both. These are estimates, but low enough to fit even the free limit again. Payment and diagnosis are done. With your OK, I'll prepare the code and one SQL file.
